glossary-term.definition: The human researcher who asks natural-language questions about an Indexed Codebase and reads the Assistant's answers.

A persisted conversation thread between one Analyst and the Assistant, identified by a stable id and an Analyst-readable title, holding the full ordered sequence of Messages exchanged in that conversation. A Session is OPEN (accepting new Messages) or CLOSED (frozen, read-only).
glossary-term.example: Session 7f3a1b2c "audit auth flow" — 24 Messages, last activity 2026-05-17.

glossary-term.definition: A single turn in a Session carrying a role (Analyst, Assistant, Tool, or System), a textual content body, an in-Session sequence number, and an optional list of Tool Call attachments. A Message is finalized once its content has been completely produced.
The system's AI helper, presented to the Analyst as "kloc analyst". Answers Analyst questions by reasoning, invoking Tools against the Indexed Codebase, and composing a natural-language reply.

A discrete capability the Assistant can invoke during a Session: a code-search or code-context function, a file reader, or a delegation to a specialised sub-Assistant. The set of Tools available is fixed at Session start.

A single Assistant-initiated invocation of a Tool, with a name, arguments, a status (in-progress, executing, or complete), and — once finished — a result body. A Tool Call may instead be denied by policy, in which case its result is a denial reason.

A Tool Call whose execution was blocked by the system's policy. The Assistant receives a denial reason in place of a tool result; the Analyst sees the denial visually distinguished from successful Tool Calls.
A named file produced by the Assistant during a Session and attached to the Session so the Analyst can refer back to it later.
The external source code that the system has pre-analysed and over which the Assistant can answer questions. The current deployment is indexed against a single PHP codebase.

A per-Session marker identifying the last event the Analyst's view has observed during an in-flight Assistant response. Used to replay missed events after a transient connection loss without duplicating already seen content.

actor.description: The Analyst is the only initiator of behavior. They browse and resume Sessions, start new Sessions, ask the Assistant questions, and observe Tool Calls and Artifacts as the Assistant works.

use-case.goal: See the list of prior Sessions in order of most-recent activity so a past conversation can be picked up.
use-case.precondition: The Analyst has visited the system's landing surface.

main-flow.step: System retrieves all of the Analyst's Sessions, most-recently-active first.
System presents each Session with its title, Message count, last-activity time, and a short identifier.
Analyst reads the list to choose a Session or to decide to start a new one.

alternative-flow.name: no-prior-sessions
alternative-flow.step: The Analyst has no prior Sessions.
System presents an empty-state indication and a prompt to start a new Session.

alternative-flow.name: retrieval-failed
alternative-flow.step: The list of Sessions cannot currently be retrieved.
System presents an error indication naming the failure cause.
The option to start a new Session remains available.

use-case.postcondition: The Analyst either sees their list of Sessions, an empty-state indication, or a retrieval-failure indication.
use-case.acceptance: Given an Analyst with three prior Sessions When they open the landing surface Then they see the three Sessions And the most-recently-updated Session appears first And each Session shows its title, Message count, and last-activity time
Given an Analyst with no prior Sessions When they open the landing surface Then they see an empty-state indication And the option to start a new Session is available

use-case.goal: Begin a fresh conversation with the Assistant about the Indexed Codebase.
use-case.precondition: The Analyst is on the landing surface.

main-flow.step: System creates a new OPEN Session and prepares it for the first Message.
System presents the conversation surface for the new Session, ready to accept the Analyst's first question.

alternative-flow.name: creation-failed
alternative-flow.step: The new Session cannot be created.
System remains on the landing surface and presents an error indication.

use-case.postcondition: An OPEN Session exists belonging to the Analyst, or the landing surface displays a creation-failure indication.
use-case.acceptance: Given the Analyst is on the landing surface When they request a new Session Then a new OPEN Session is created And the conversation surface for that Session opens And the conversation has zero prior Messages

use-case.goal: Continue a prior conversation from exactly where it left off, with the earlier Messages visible alongside the live conversation.
use-case.precondition: At least one prior Session exists for the Analyst.

main-flow.step: Analyst selects a Session from their list.
System retrieves the Session's prior Messages in order.
System presents the conversation surface for the selected Session and indicates that prior Messages will appear in the conversation when the next Message is sent.

alternative-flow.name: prior-history-too-large
alternative-flow.step: The Session has more prior Messages than can be retrieved in a single page.
System presents the most recent page and indicates that older Messages exist.

use-case.postcondition: The Analyst is positioned on the conversation surface for the chosen Session with its prior history accessible.
use-case.acceptance: Given a Session with five prior Messages When the Analyst selects that Session from the list Then the conversation surface for that Session opens And an indication shows that five prior Messages will appear when the next Message is sent
Given the Analyst has chosen a Session When the conversation surface opens Then the Analyst can return to the Session list without losing the chosen Session's state

use-case.goal: Ask a natural-language question about the Indexed Codebase and observe the Assistant's reply as it is produced, including any Tool Calls and Artifacts the Assistant generates.
use-case.precondition: An OPEN Session has been picked or just created.
The Analyst has typed a question into the conversation surface.

main-flow.step: System records the Analyst's Message in the Session before forwarding it to the Assistant.

System presents a pending Assistant indicator in the conversation — carrying the Assistant's identity and an active progress affordance — so the Analyst sees that a reply is being prepared before any content has been emitted.
System begins streaming the Assistant's reply: textual content appears progressively as it is generated, replacing the pending indicator.

For each Tool the Assistant invokes, System presents a Tool Call indicator showing the Tool name, the arguments, and a live status; on completion, the Tool Call's result is attached to that indicator.
For each Artifact the Assistant produces, System surfaces it as a named entry visible alongside the conversation.
System finalizes the Assistant's Message when its content is complete.

alternative-flow.name: tool-denied
alternative-flow.step: A Tool Call requested by the Assistant is blocked by the system's policy.
System presents the Tool Call indicator as a Tool Denial, distinguished visually from completed Tool Calls, and shows the denial reason.
The Assistant receives the denial reason in place of a tool result and continues its reply.

alternative-flow.name: session-closed
alternative-flow.step: The Session has been CLOSED.
System rejects the submission with a clear "this Session is closed" indication.
No Message is appended; no Assistant reply is generated.

alternative-flow.name: assistant-failed
alternative-flow.step: The Assistant cannot produce a reply due to a system fault.
System indicates the failure to the Analyst and preserves the Analyst's already-recorded Message.

use-case.postcondition: If the reply completed: the Session contains the Analyst's Message and the Assistant's finalized Message in order, along with any Tool Calls and Artifacts produced. If the reply failed: the Analyst's Message is still recorded; the Assistant's Message is absent or marked unfinalized.
use-case.acceptance: Given an OPEN Session and a typed question When the Analyst submits the question Then the question is recorded as a Message in the Session And the Assistant's reply text appears progressively And the reply Message is finalized once its content is complete

Given an OPEN Session and a typed question When the Analyst submits the question Then a pending Assistant indicator appears in the conversation carrying the Assistant's identity and an active progress affordance And no separate connection-status banner is shown for this waiting state And the pending indicator is replaced once the Assistant's first piece of content (text, Tool Call, or Artifact) arrives

Given the Assistant is replying When it invokes a Tool to search the Indexed Codebase Then a Tool Call indicator appears in the conversation And the indicator reflects the Tool's status as it runs And on completion the Tool's result is attached to the indicator

Given the Assistant attempts a Tool Call When the system's policy blocks that Tool Call Then a Tool Denial indicator appears in the conversation And the denial reason is visible to the Analyst And the indicator is visually distinct from a successful Tool Call
Given the Assistant produces an Artifact during its reply When the Artifact is attached to the Session Then the Analyst sees the Artifact's name surfaced alongside the conversation

use-case.goal: Pick up an in-flight Assistant reply where it left off when a transient connection loss has occurred, without losing any reply content produced while disconnected.
use-case.precondition: The Analyst was observing an Assistant reply in an OPEN Session.
The Analyst's connection to the system was interrupted while the reply was still in progress.

main-flow.step: System retains the Stream Cursor for the last event the Analyst's view observed.
When the Analyst reconnects, System replays events produced during the disconnect, from the Stream Cursor onwards.
System resumes live streaming once the replay is current.

alternative-flow.name: reply-already-completed
alternative-flow.step: The Assistant finished its reply while the Analyst was disconnected.
On reconnect, System delivers the remaining events of that reply and then idles, ready for the Analyst's next question.

alternative-flow.name: recovery-window-exceeded
alternative-flow.step: The Analyst remained disconnected longer than the system retains streaming context.
System shows the prior Messages of the Session (including any finalized Assistant Message) and does not replay intermediate streaming events.

use-case.postcondition: The conversation surface reflects the Session's current state, including all Messages, Tool Calls, and Artifacts produced while the Analyst was disconnected.
use-case.acceptance: Given an Analyst is observing an in-flight Assistant reply When the Analyst's connection drops momentarily And the Analyst reconnects within the recovery window Then the events emitted during the disconnect are replayed And live streaming resumes from the current point And no Tool Call or Artifact produced during the disconnect is missing

Given the Assistant finishes its reply while the Analyst is disconnected When the Analyst reconnects Then the finalized Assistant Message is visible And the Session is idle and ready for the next question

spec.rule: The system shall record every Message in its Session in the order in which it was created, with a per-Session sequence number that strictly increases.
When the Analyst submits a question, the system shall record the Analyst's Message in the Session before requesting the Assistant's reply.
The system shall present the Assistant's reply progressively as it is generated; the Analyst shall see partial content before the reply is complete.

While the Analyst is awaiting the Assistant's first piece of visible content for the most recently submitted question — that is, after the question has been recorded and before any text, Tool Call, or Artifact has appeared in the conversation — the system shall display a pending Assistant indicator inside the conversation carrying the Assistant's identity ("kloc analyst") and an active progress affordance, and shall not surface a separate connection-status banner for this waiting state. The pending indicator shall be replaced as soon as the Assistant's first piece of visible content arrives.

When the Assistant invokes a Tool, the system shall display a Tool Call indicator carrying the Tool's name, arguments, and live status, and shall attach the Tool's result to that indicator on completion.
When a Tool Call is blocked by policy, the system shall present it as a Tool Denial visually distinct from completed Tool Calls and shall show the denial reason.
If a Session has been CLOSED, then the system shall not accept any further Message on that Session.
When the Analyst reconnects to an in-flight Assistant reply within the recovery window, the system shall replay every event produced after the Analyst's Stream Cursor before resuming live emission.
While the Analyst is on the conversation surface of a Session that has prior Messages, the system shall make those prior Messages accessible to the Analyst.
When the Assistant attaches an Artifact to a Session, the system shall surface the Artifact's name to the Analyst alongside the conversation.

Every TOOL_CALL_START AG-UI event (and every CUSTOM { name: ToolCallDenied } event) emitted during an Assistant turn shall carry a parentMessageId equal to the messageId of the most-recent TEXT_MESSAGE_START within that run. Tool calls that arrive without parentMessageId shall be dropped by the frontend reducer with a console warning; the runner is the source of truth.

Skill bodies under `<available_skills>` in the system prompt are loaded in full. The orchestrator MUST NOT issue a `file_read` whose target is a `SKILL.md` file already inlined in the prompt; doing so wastes a turn and re-fetches content the model already has.

When the Analyst names a project (`kyc`, `order-api`, …) AND references a file path, the orchestrator MUST call `read_project_file(project_name=..., path=...)` to fetch byte-exact content before quoting it. `kloc_source` / `kloc_chunks` remain preferred for chunked indexed PHP; `read_project_file` is the tool for byte-exact ranges, non-PHP files, and files outside the index.
The system shall present to the Analyst only the Sessions belonging to that Analyst.

invariant.statement: For any Session, the sequence numbers of its Messages are unique and strictly increasing from the first Message to the most recent.
invariant.rationale: Conversation ordering is foundational; out-of-order Messages corrupt the Analyst's mental model and break any downstream replay.

invariant.statement: For every finalized Assistant Message in a Session, an earlier Analyst Message exists in the same Session.
invariant.rationale: The Assistant only responds to questions; an Assistant Message with no preceding question indicates lost durability of the Analyst's input.

invariant.statement: No Message exists in any Session whose creation time is later than that Session's closure time.
Any Tool Call presented to the Analyst as denied is visually distinguishable from any Tool Call presented as completed, in colour and label.
Every Artifact surfaced to the Analyst has a human-readable filename.

event.name: SessionCreated
event.description: A new OPEN Session has been created for the Analyst.

event.name: SessionResumed
event.description: The Analyst has reopened a prior Session and its history has been retrieved for display.

event.name: MessageSubmitted
event.description: The Analyst has submitted a question. The Message has been recorded in its Session in advance of any Assistant work.

event.name: AssistantResponseStarted
event.description: The Assistant has begun composing a reply to the Analyst's most recent Message.

event.name: ToolCallStarted
event.description: The Assistant has invoked a Tool; the Analyst sees an in-progress indicator carrying the Tool's name and arguments.

event.name: ToolCallCompleted
event.description: A previously started Tool Call has returned a result; the Analyst's indicator now shows the result.

event.name: ToolCallDenied
event.description: A previously started Tool Call has been blocked by policy; the Analyst's indicator now shows the denial reason in a distinct visual style.

event.name: ArtifactAttached
event.description: The Assistant has produced an Artifact and attached it to the Session for the Analyst's reference.

event.name: AssistantResponseCompleted
event.description: The Assistant's reply has been finalized; no further content will be appended to that Message.

event.name: StreamResumed
event.description: The Analyst has reconnected after a transient interruption and missed events have been replayed up to the live point.

scenario.stimulus: Selects a Session with hundreds of prior Messages
scenario.environment: Conversation surface opening for a chosen Session
scenario.response: The most recent prior Messages are presented
scenario.response-measure: up to 500 Messages are retrieved in a single page

scenario.stimulus: Submits a question to the Assistant
scenario.response: The first piece of the Assistant's reply becomes visible
scenario.response-measure: within 1000 ms at p95 from submission to first visible token

scenario.stimulus: Reconnects within the recovery window after a transient drop
scenario.environment: An in-flight Assistant reply is in progress
scenario.response: Missed events are replayed; live streaming resumes without loss
scenario.response-measure: at least 99.9% of reconnects within the recovery window restore the conversation without missing events

scenario.stimulus: Observes a Tool Denial in the conversation
scenario.response: The Tool Denial is conveyed by both colour and a label, not by colour alone
scenario.response-measure: denial state is identifiable by users who cannot distinguish colour differences

scenario.response: The document declares its natural language for assistive technology
scenario.response-measure: document language attribute is present and correct
